subject: english
title: The Parrot Who Wouldn't Talk
author: Ruskin Bond
instructions: Literature practice for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Identify the following sentences as True or False.

questions.q: Aunt Ruby's parrot was very fond of Aunt Ruby.
The narrator deliberately set the parrot free.
Aunt Ruby's parrot used to talk a lot to everyone.
Granny and Grandfather were keen on keeping caged birds.
The parrot knocked Aunt Ruby's spectacles off her nose.
In the end the parrot repeated Aunt Ruby's own words.

sections.title: Match the character (or speaker) with the description.

questions.right: taunted the parrot: 'Can't talk, can't sing, can't dance!'
questions.answer: Aunt Ruby — taunted the parrot: 'Can't talk, can't sing, can't dance!'

questions.right: sold caged birds from house to house
questions.answer: A bird-catcher — sold caged birds from house to house

questions.right: a ten-year-old boy who set the parrot free
questions.answer: The narrator — a ten-year-old boy who set the parrot free

questions.right: offered Aunt Ruby a gramophone instead of a bird
questions.answer: Grandfather — offered Aunt Ruby a gramophone instead of a bird

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The parrot was bought by ________ from a bird-catcher.
Granny and Grandfather weren't keen on keeping ________ birds as pets.
Aunt Ruby's tantrums were ________ to behold.

sections.passage: He'd been bought by Aunt Ruby from a bird-catcher who'd visited all the houses on our road, selling caged birds ranging from colourful budgerigars to chirpy little munnias and even common sparrows that had been dabbed with paint and passed off as some exotic species. Neither Granny nor Grandfather were keen on keeping caged birds as pets, but Aunt Ruby threatened to throw a tantrum if she did not get her way — and Aunt Ruby's tantrums were dreadful to behold!

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Everyone was indoors enjoying a ________.
The narrator ________ left the cage door open.
The bird flew to the freedom of the mango ________.

sections.passage: One afternoon, while everyone was indoors enjoying a siesta, I gave the parrot its lunch and then deliberately left the cage door open. Seconds later, the bird was winging its way to the freedom of the mango orchard.

questions.q: The narrator fed the parrot green ________ and ripe tomatoes.
Aunt Ruby used to say, 'You're no ________!'
After the parrot flew away, Aunt Ruby was promised ________ instead — 'But they don't talk!'
When the parrot repeated her words, Aunt Ruby went ________.

sections.title: Answer in one or two sentences (about 30 words).

questions.q: What happens when the parrot returns and sees Aunt Ruby?
questions.answer: It flies out of her reach to a rose bush and shrieks in her own voice, 'You're no beauty! Can't talk, can't sing, can't dance!'

questions.q: How did the parrot escape its cage?
questions.answer: The narrator deliberately left the cage door open after feeding it while everyone was having a siesta, and it flew away to the mango orchard.

questions.q: Why did the parrot back away from Aunt Ruby?
questions.answer: It disliked her and did not want to be kissed by her when she cooed 'Kiss, kiss!'

questions.q: What made Aunt Ruby go ruby-red?
questions.answer: The parrot she had taunted repeated her own insulting words back to her: 'You're no beauty! Can't talk, can't sing, can't dance!'

questions.q: Why did the parrot come back a few days later?
questions.answer: It probably missed the green chillies (and mangoes) the narrator used to feed it.

questions.q: What pets did Indians and Europeans keep in those days and what were the specialities of the birds?
questions.answer: Almost everyone kept a pet parrot, parakeet or 'lovebird'. Some became great talkers or mimics and learnt to recite whole mantras or advice to the children of the house, like 'Padho beta, padho!' or 'Don't be greedy!', picked up after many repetitions.

or.q: How did the parrot finally 'learn to talk'? What is ironic about it?
or.answer: Aunt Ruby kept taunting it, 'You're no beauty! Can't talk, can't sing, can't dance!' The parrot picked up these very words, and after its escape it shouted them at her whenever it saw her. The irony is that the only words it learnt were the insults meant for it, now turned against Aunt Ruby.
